APARTMENT REZONINGS: MORE VISIBILITY.

Austin is setting up a monthly tracking process for rezoning applications involving existing multifamily properties.

An Austin Housing memo dated October 30 outlines how Planning staff will send a case list for the Community Development Commission’s monthly meeting, giving commissioners an opportunity to review, discuss and recommend action to City Council.

The list will have two parts: newly received cases involving existing apartments, and active cases that have not received final Council action. Cases will remain listed until Council considers them.

Planning staff will send the chart to Housing staff two weeks before each CDC meeting, with timing subject to holidays and City closures.

For renters, owners and neighbors, the practical value is another place to follow proposed zoning changes affecting existing apartment properties.

This process does not approve a rezoning or create a new tenant benefit. The CDC can make recommendations; Council retains the decision. The memo also specifies that Austin Housing staff will not recommend for or against individual applications.

Source: Austin Housing memo, October 30, 2026, posted November 2.
